description: HTTP header names and prefixes with Ferrum Edge semantics: gateway assertions, diagnostic response headers, internal markers, mesh control headers, and admin API headers, including standard HTTP ETag and If-Match. Names and prefixes match case-insensitively. Availability records the first Edge tag containing the surface. From Edge v0.9.15 the gateway writes its request assertions after it has resolved a client's Connection nominations at HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/3 ingress; the src/proxy/headers.rs provenance note gives the rule.

provenance.note: Connection nominations (ferrum-edge#6090, issue #6087, from v0.9.15): HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/3 ingress removes every field a client's Connection header nominates before any plugin runs, and rewrites Connection to keep only the close option and the request hop-by-hop names connection, keep-alive, proxy-authorization, proxy-connection, te, trailer, transfer-encoding and upgrade. Host, Content-Length, Expect, Forwarded, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Host, X-Forwarded-Port, X-Forwarded-Proto, X-Real-IP and the configured FERRUM_REAL_IP_HEADER are protected and keep their client values for routing, framing and trusted-proxy client-IP resolution. A nominated Authorization is removed before authentication. Gateway assertions (consumer identity, X-Authenticated-Identity, claim_headers destinations, X-Geo-Country, path-param captures) and transformer-added headers are written afterwards, so a client nomination cannot remove them. HTTP/2 rejects Connection and is unchanged. Gateway-owned assertion names match ASCII case-insensitively with _ equivalent to - (field_names_equivalent_for_backends), the folding CGI-style backends apply.

headers.name: X-Consumer-Username
headers.edge_behavior: Set by the gateway only after a principal is resolved; never trusted from clients. Any client copy is removed before dispatch. From v0.9.15 (ferrum-edge#6088, issue #6082) the value is only the username of a gateway Consumer that the authentication flow mapped. An external identity or display claim without a mapped Consumer is sent as X-Authenticated-Identity instead, and external authentication no longer maps a principal to a Consumer by matching a username, ID or custom ID. Up to v0.9.14 this header fell back to the external display identity, then the raw external identity.

headers.name: X-Authenticated-Identity
headers.edge_behavior: Gateway-owned external identity header (ferrum-edge#6088, issue #6082). Set only when a request authenticated without a mapped gateway Consumer: the provider's display claim when one is configured and present, otherwise the external authenticated identity. For jwks_auth and oauth2_introspection the display claim is the provider consumer_header_claim, then the global consumer_header_claim, then the provider's effective consumer_identity_claim. An unverified display value, not a gateway-verified Consumer assertion; backends must not treat it as proof of a mapped Consumer. Never sent with X-Consumer-Username, and not sent when a plugin suppresses consumer identity headers. Matching is ASCII case-insensitive with _ equivalent to -: client copies are removed before any plugin runs and plugin copies are scrubbed before dispatch, on every protocol path, and the name is forbidden in request trailers. Refused as a configured header destination at config load (request_transformer, claim_headers, Gateway API RequestHeaderModifier and similar header mutation rules).
